- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.5) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- If model shows sharp upward spike followed by forecast overshoot, cap peak forecast at 2–3% below true peak.
- In low sentiment (≤0.2) periods, model underestimates; add 1–2% to forecast to compensate for mean reversion bias.
- If true outcome exceeds forecast by >5% for 2+ consecutive days, adjust future forecasts downward by 0.5–1% per day to avoid overcorrection.
- For 30-day horizon, model often lags true trend by 2–4 days; shift forecast 1–2 days ahead if sentiment is rising.
- If sentiment history shows alternating highs/lows (e.g., 0.8, 0.2, 0.8), model tends to misalign with sentiment cycles; align forecast slope with sentiment direction.
